title: A specified scalar resolution gives compatible local derived matrix models
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $S$, and a small site $(C,J)$ equivalent to $S_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ with its induced topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the concrete rings, functors, complexes and maps of [def-sp-integral-matrix-model-data]. Let $L$ be a $B$-module sheaf. Let $U\in C$ and let $N$ be a finitely presented $A$-module such that $L|_U\simeq(B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline N)|_U$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Given any finite matrix $d:A^a\to A^b$ and $p:A^b\to N$ with $d$ injective, $\operatorname{im}(d)=\ker(p)$ and $p$ surjective, there is an isomorphism $e_N:(B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline N)|_U\simeq L|_U$ such that the realized sequence $d,p$ composed with $e_N$ is short exact, and $\operatorname{SimultaneousModels}(L,U,d)$ is inhabited. This statement makes no assertion about quotient cohomology, finite residues, global vanishing, or covering sieves.

proof.text: First compare reduction with restriction to a covering object $U$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to L[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat], $P|_U$ is K-flat and restriction is exact, so it resolves $L|_U[0]$. The pure-tensor comparison of [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], termwise with $B_n$ in degree zero, identifies $(P\otimes_B B_n)|_U$ with $P|_U\otimes_{B_U}(B_n)|_U$; the differentials agree by naturality. Applying [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to these two resolutions proves $(L[0]\otimes_B^LB_n)|_U\cong L|_U[0]\otimes_{B_U}^L(B_n)|_U$ in the localized coefficient derived category. This argument uses the actual restricted ring $B_U$, not a newly pulled-back completion; it is natural for every coefficient quotient map, since the tensor comparisons send $x\otimes a$ to $x\otimes a$.

source.place: Tag 0E8K (lemma-restriction-K-flat); Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), localized coefficient tensor comparison

proof.text: Start with the given injective matrix d, exact augmentation p and surjectivity of p. The exact constant functor of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact] makes this an exact sequence on $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] for $I=(\ell)$, extension to $B$ is exact. Restrict this sequence to $U$ using [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat]. Tensor restriction [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] identifies its last term with the specified $B_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline N\cong L|_U$. Its free terms are $B_U^u,B_U^v$: the mutually inverse identifications send $b\otimes(a_i)$ to $(ba_i)$ and $(b_i)$ to $\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$. Thus the differential is the single scalar matrix $d$, independent of $n$.

source.place: Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact), 093M (lemma-completion-flat); more-algebra.tex Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), scalar kernel resolution

proof.text: Put $K=[B_U^u\xrightarrow d B_U^v]$ in degrees $-1,0$ with its specified augmentation to $L|_U[0]$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-finite-free-resolution-tensor] this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and $K$ is K-flat with flat terms. Derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] therefore computes reduction in $D((B_n)_U)$ by $K\otimes_{B_U}(B_n)_U$. The free-basis tensor formulas in [lem-sfb-ringed-finite-free-resolution-tensor] identify its terms with $(B_n)_U^u,(B_n)_U^v$ and its differential with $(z_i)\mapsto(\sum_i\overline d_{ki}z_i)_k$. Since $(B_n)_U=\underline{A_n}_U$, this is the asserted constant matrix complex. Combined with step 1 it represents the originally stated restricted derived object, not merely its cohomology.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); fixed two-term matrix computation

proof.text: For $m\le n$ let $q_{nm}:(B_n)_U\to(B_m)_U$ be the specified coefficient quotient [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Keep this same augmented $K$ for every level. On this K-flat representative the quotient-induced arrow is $1_K\otimes q_{nm}$: the normalized extension unit and its adjunct are respectively $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Taking $g(x)=x\otimes1$ at level $m$ gives $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes q_{nm}(a)$. Under the basis identifications this is entrywise reduction on both terms. It is a chain map since $q_{nm}(\overline d_{ki}z)=\overline d_{ki}\,q_{nm}(z)$, and the quotient maps compose strictly. Thus the derived identifications respect all actual transitions simultaneously on the original cover, including identity transitions.
